name: PCV (procarbazine, lomustine, vinCRIStine)
histology: IDH-mutant astrocytoma, 1p/19q non-codeleted (WHO CNS grade 2 or 3)

biomarkers.1p_19q: non-codeleted (codeletion would reclassify as oligodendroglioma; see cns-oligodendroglioma-pcv)
biomarkers.note: PCV is given after radiotherapy for IDH-mutant astrocytoma; temozolomide is the alternative systemic option. 1p/19q non-codeletion distinguishes astrocytoma from oligodendroglioma. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), CNS Cancers, Principles of Brain Tumor Pathology (BRAIN-E) and the astrocytoma pathway.

lineOfTherapy: first-line adjuvant systemic therapy after radiotherapy

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: PCV administered after radiotherapy (adjuvant), not before
eligibilityCriteria.locator: GLIO footnote (PCV after RT, per EORTC 26951), cns.txt line 721 to 722

drugs.name: Lomustine (CCNU)

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

drugs.notes: 110 mg/m2 by mouth on day 1. Nitrosourea myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia earlier and more severe than leukopenia) is cumulative and delayed; hematopoietic recovery may be incomplete even at 6-week intervals, and cumulative doses above 1,000 mg/m2 add pulmonary and marrow toxicity. Sources: DeVita 12th ed., devita.txt line 237647 (dose), lines 15373 and 15407 (cumulative myelosuppression).

drugs.name: Procarbazine

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: devita.txt line 237646 (procarbazine 60 mg/m2 x 14 days, days 8 to 21)

drugs.notes: 60 mg/m2 by mouth daily on days 8 to 21 (14 days). Procarbazine is a weak MAO inhibitor with a disulfiram-like reaction to alcohol; counsel on tyramine and alcohol. Source: DeVita 12th ed., devita.txt line 237646.

drugs.name: vinCRIStine

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: devita.txt line 237648 (vincristine 1.4 mg/m2, maximum total 2 mg, day 8 and day 29)

drugs.notes: 1.4 mg/m2 IV on days 8 and 29, capped at a maximum total of 2 mg per dose (ISMP tall-man vinCRIStine; fatal if given intrathecally, IV only). In current adult practice vincristine is often omitted from PCV because of overlapping myelosuppression, cumulative peripheral neuropathy, and poor blood-brain-barrier penetration (physician decision). Source: DeVita 12th ed., devita.txt line 237648 (dose and 2 mg cap) and following paragraph (omission in practice).

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: lomustine and procarbazine are moderately to highly emetogenic on dosing days; give 5-HT3 antagonist prophylaxis.

supportiveCare: monitor for cumulative and delayed nitrosourea myelosuppression across cycles (nadir platelets can be late; track cumulative lomustine dose)
procarbazine: avoid alcohol (disulfiram-like reaction) and tyramine-rich foods (weak MAO inhibition)
vinCRIStine: IV only, never intrathecal; monitor peripheral neuropathy and constipation

monitoring: CBC with platelets before each cycle and at the delayed nitrosourea nadir
peripheral neuropathy assessment before each vinCRIStine dose
cumulative lomustine dose tracking (pulmonary and marrow toxicity)

doseModificationRules.condition: delayed thrombocytopenia or neutropenia at cycle start
doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Nitrosourea nadir is delayed; confirm count recovery before the next cycle and reduce lomustine for cumulative myelosuppression. Physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: CNS chapter, devita.txt lines 237646 to 237648 (PCV component doses); lines 15373 and 15407 (nitrosourea cumulative myelosuppression)

guideline.locator: Astrocytoma pathway (RT then adjuvant PCV or temozolomide); GLIO footnote (PCV after RT per EORTC 26951, cns.txt lines 721 to 722); carmustine may substitute for lomustine (footnote c, cns.txt line 1395)

provenanceNote: PCV component doses are grounded in DeVita 12th ed. (devita.txt lines 237646 to 237648): procarbazine 60 mg/m2 by mouth days 8 to 21, lomustine (CCNU) 110 mg/m2 by mouth day 1, and vinCRIStine 1.4 mg/m2 IV days 8 and 29 with a maximum total of 2 mg per dose (ISMP tall-man cap enforced). Six cycles reflect the guideline PCV x 6 schedule (cns.txt line 654) and PCV is given after radiotherapy (cns.txt lines 721 to 722). cycleLengthDays is left VERIFY because the cited sources give the per-drug day schedule (vinCRIStine on day 29 implies a cycle of at least 29 days, historically a 6-week cycle) but do not print an explicit cycle interval; this must be resolved before ACTIVE. The lomustine warn threshold (1000 mg/m2 cumulative) is source-grounded in the nitrosourea cumulative-toxicity discussion (devita.txt lines 15373 and 15407, added pulmonary and marrow toxicity above 1,000 mg/m2); the 1100 mg/m2 hard stop is a StewardMD institutional safety margin above that threshold and is not printed in the source. No dose value was invented. No hospital or endorsement claim. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
